component.name: cheatu
component.summary: Memory scanner and cheat tool for Linux

description.p: cheatu is a memory scanner for Linux, inspired by Cheat Engine and scanmem. Attach to a running process (games in particular), search for values, narrow the results as those values change, and then edit or freeze them.
It ships as one engine behind two front-ends:

ul.li: cheatu — a scanmem-style interactive command line.
cheatu-gui — a graphical UI (egui/eframe) that runs natively on both Wayland and Xorg, and looks the same under KDE, GNOME, and standalone window managers with no GTK or Qt dependency.

description.p: A dedicated RPG Maker MV/MZ (NW.js) mode uses JavaScript injection through the engine's own data model, which is stable where raw memory freezing is not.

Scanning: search a range of values when you can only bracket a number, scan for an unknown value as every type at once, and cancel a running scan — which now reports its progress. Large unknown-value scans are refused up front instead of exhausting memory.
Results: sort the results table, and probe every visible candidate in one pass to see which address the game overwrites.
Cheat table: write a value once without freezing it, and watch each address's live value as you do.
Initial release: multithreaded memory scanner (CLI + GUI) and the RPG Maker MV/MZ JavaScript-injection backend.
